column1: # Macros: matching, capitalisation and English mode (C-009, plan §3 row 9).
# The sixth column is the case's macro table, `name=content;name=content`.
# It is literal UTF-8 with no escape decoding, the first `=` splits a pair, and
# `-` (or an absent column) is the empty table. A duplicate name is legal
# Every expected value below was produced by the pinned harness
# (scripts/parity/harness.cpp) for the row as written; none is hand-computed.
# The live path: `use_macro` defaults to 1, so a table is enough.
# Negative control for the row above: the same input against no table at all is
# the raw typed text. Without this pair a pass could come from the input alone.
# And the explicit empty table, so the `-` spelling of "none" is exercised too.
# A macro ends on the macro break codes, not only on space (Engine.cpp:1329);
# the break key itself is typed afterwards (OpenKey.mm:574).
# A backspace shortens the tracked key, so `kob` + backspace is `ko` again
# The table is inert with the feature off.
# English mode: the Vietnamese engine never runs, only the macro matcher
# upperCaseFirstCharacter writes the caps bit into the tracked key, which is
# what lets a new sentence match a lowercase macro (Engine.cpp:1051).
# Content is free text: spaces and capitals survive.
# An empty content still deletes the typed key and keeps the break key.
# The first match consumes the key, so the second space is just a space
# The table is keyed on keycodes, so a VNI case types its name as VNI.
# Duplicate names replace, and only the first `=` splits a pair.
